subject: food-technology
title: Food Provenance & Sustainability: Application
welcome_lead: Apply ideas about farming systems, animal welfare and food waste.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE provenance: intensive vs extensive farming, food waste, plant-based.
final_note: Every dietary choice is also an environmental choice.

concepts.def: High-yield farming using lots of inputs.
Low-density farming using more land, fewer inputs.
Animals have outdoor access for part of life.
Diet largely or fully based on plant foods.
Edible food thrown away rather than eaten.
Greenhouse gases linked to producing a food.

walkthroughs.body_html: Intensive farming produces lots of food per hectare using fertilisers, pesticides and high-density livestock — cheaper but with welfare and environmental costs. Extensive farming uses more land per animal, often higher welfare but lower yields.

Animal protein has a higher carbon footprint than most plant protein. Shifting partly to a plant-based diet — beans, lentils, tofu — cuts emissions and is associated with lower rates of heart disease.

UK households throw away around 6.6 million tonnes of food a year, most of it edible. Plan meals, store food correctly, freeze leftovers and use up older items first. Reducing food waste is one of the biggest single carbon cuts you can make.
